content.text: Characterized by bilateral cystic ovaries, insulin resistance, & hyperandrogenism
increased LH leads to increased testosterone production
decreased FSH leads to follicular degeneration & bilateral cystic ovaries
metabolic syndrome, DM, CVD, dyslipidemia, endometrial hyperplasia, endometrial cancer
– coarse hair on face, neck, & abdomen, acne, male pattern baldness
bilateral enlarged, smooth, mobile ovaries on bimanual exam, acanthosis nigricans
•lab or clinical signs (hirsutism, acne, male pattern baldness)
•Anti-androgenic agents: spironolactone (can be added to OCPs of sxs persist after 6mo)
toxic shock syndrome toxin is a superantigen that activates a large number of T cells, which releases various inflammatory mediators (IL-2, IL-1, TNF)
– this causes capillary leakage, circulatory collapse, & multi-organ failure
•surgical and postpartum wound infections, burns, & contraceptive sponge use
Sudden onset high fever (≥102.2F), tachycardia, N/V/D, pharyngitis
diffuse erythematous macular rash (resembles sunburn, includes palms & soles), desquamation
: hospital admin, removal of offending object,
•vancomycin: 30mg/kg IV per day (divide into 2 daily doses)
